question: close_session does not rotate session_id — architectural review needed. close_session (server.py:2137-2211) currently records a reflection insight, optionally records surprise + handoff, increments reflection_depth, advances spiral phase, and calls save_spiral_state — but never touches the session_id field. Only SpiralState.__init__ rotates the session_id (called by spiral_inherit). This caused chronicle metadata to silently freeze at session_id='test-session-hook-777' from 2026-04-22 to 2026-04-29 across all MCP-tool writes, despite multiple close_session calls during that window. The 2026-04-29 morning fix was a one-shot spiral_inherit() call (Tony-iPhone-HQ orchestrated diagnosis). The deeper question for an architectural review: should close_session imply session_id rotation? Spiral semantics suggest one cycle COHERENCE_CHECK→INITIALIZATION = one completed session — at which point a new session_id makes sense. But that conflates 'closed phase cycle' with 'closed working session,' which may not always be what callers want. Alternatives: (a) auto-rotate on COHERENCE_CHECK→INITIALIZATION transition; (b) add an explicit rotate_session_id arg to close_session; (c) add a separate rotate_session primitive. Don't propose a fix here; just naming the gap so a future RFC can pick it up. Found by claude-iphone orchestration brief 2026-04-29.
resolution: Documented as intentional non-rotation. close_session advances spiral phase but does NOT rotate session_id — that requires explicit spiral_inherit(). Added this to the tool description and appended a rotation_note to every close_session output reminding callers to call spiral_inherit() to start a genuinely new session. commit 23e10aa.
